blocks.prompt: 9 Given that: \(\int_{0}^{9} f(x)\,dx = 16\) and \(\int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx = 12\). Evaluate the integral \(\int_{3}^{9} \big(2f(x) + 5\big)\,dx\).
blocks.explanation:
Two steps: first find \(\int_3^9 f\) from the given values (Property III), then use linearity.
Property IX splits \(\int (2f + 5)\) into \(2\int f + \int 5\).
\(\int_3^9 5\,dx\) is just 5 times the length of the interval.
steps:
Given: \(\int_{0}^{9} f(x)\,dx = 16\), \(\int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx = 12\).
To find: \(\int_{3}^{9} \big(2f(x) + 5\big)\,dx\).
Method: Property III to get \(\int_3^9 f\); Property IX \(\int (\alpha f_1 + \beta f_2) = \alpha\int f_1 + \beta\int f_2\).

Split the required integral
\[\int_{3}^{9} \big(2f(x) + 5\big)\,dx = 2\int_{3}^{9} f(x)\,dx + \int_{3}^{9} 5\,dx\]
Why: Property IX.

Check
\[2(4) + 5(6) = 38 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the constant 5 over an interval of length 6 adds 30; the key prints 38.
